methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College partners with Google for free AI training - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Free Google AI training at Roanoke College creates peer-to-peer learning infrastructure outside metro hubs, potentially seeding distributed capability if participants activate local networks rather than migrate to NoVA.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Grassroots AI workshops led by a Norfolk native targeting the 'technology gap' represents community-driven skill distribution, though sustainability depends on whether shallow exposure converts to deep practice networks.

signals.title: Virginia Tech sets course for human-centered AI leadership - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's institutional AI leadership initiative concentrates research depth in Blacksburg while the 'human-centered' framing suggests potential for statewide extension programs—outcome depends on whether knowledge stays academic or distributes practically.

signals.title: UVA study explores the role of Artificial Intelligence in special education - WVIR
signals.signal_reading: UVA's AI-in-special-education study signals platform-delivered solutions that could achieve broad distribution across Virginia school systems, but risks shallow adoption if educators become consumers rather than co-creators of AI tools.

signals.title: Camp Welcomes Hampton Roads Youth to Learn About Cybersecurity and AI - Old Dominion University
signals.signal_reading: Youth cybersecurity/AI camp at Old Dominion builds foundational fluency in Hampton Roads' next generation, creating potential distributed capability if region retains talent rather than training future NoVA workers.
